title: Lisbon vs Barcelona: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Lisbon and Barcelona based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

faqs.question: Is Lisbon or Barcelona cheaper to visit?
faqs.answer: Lisbon is significantly cheaper — expect to spend around €80–100/day on a mid-range budget, versus €120–150/day in Barcelona. faqs.question: Which city is safer for tourists, Lisbon or Barcelona?
faqs.answer: Lisbon is consistently rated safer. Barcelona has a well-documented pickpocket problem — La Rambla and the metro are notorious, and Reddit threads regularly warn about bag snatching and phone grabs. faqs.answer: Both are world-class, but in different directions. faqs.question: How far is Sintra from Lisbon, and is it worth a day trip?
faqs.answer: Sintra is 40 minutes by train from Rossio station for €2.35 each way. Absolutely worth a full day — the Palácio Nacional da Pena alone is a UNESCO World Heritage Site set on a forested mountain with views to the Atlantic. faqs.question: What is the best time of year to visit Lisbon vs Barcelona?
faqs.answer: Both cities peak in May–June and September–October when weather is warm but not oppressively hot. Barcelona's July–August hits 30–35°C with massive crowds and inflated prices. faqs.question: Is Barcelona worth visiting just for Gaudí architecture?
faqs.answer: Yes, without question. The Sagrada Família alone — a cathedral under construction since 1882 that will be completed around 2026 — is one of the most extraordinary buildings on earth. faqs.answer: Yes — they're 2 hours apart by flight (Lisbon LIS to Barcelona BCN, from €30–50 on TAP/Vueling). A 10–12 day trip could cover 4 days in Lisbon (plus a Sintra day trip), 2 nights in Porto, then 4 days in Barcelona.
